subject: Learning Methods
title: Step Three: Simplify with Analogies
description: A 60-second lesson on Step Three: Simplify with Analogies.

hook.text: Einstein said: explain it to your grandmother. If your analogy doesn't work for a novice, you haven't found the right.

buildup.text: Analogies map unfamiliar concepts onto familiar ones. The brain learns new ideas by connecting them to existing schemas.

discovery.text: Good analogies capture the structure of the concept, not the surface. 'Electricity is like water in pipes' works.

twist.text: Every analogy eventually breaks down. Knowing where it breaks is advanced understanding that deepens your knowledge.

climax.text: For each concept, create an analogy. Then ask: where does this analogy fail? The failure point reveals deeper structure.

punchline.text: Build an analogy. Then break it. Both steps teach.

quiz.question: Why is finding where an analogy breaks down useful?
options: It shows the analogy was poorly chosen
The failure point reveals deeper structure of the concept
Broken analogies confuse students and should be avoided
